step0.question: How was the recorded page region of UNIT-3B obtained, and what does the record store?
answer: It was not computed and it was not read from a text layer. The four numbers [596, 390, 644, 409] are
the lead's estimate, read off the wide K4b crop and written into the K4c task file. The K4c worker
rendered that estimate at 4 times, measured how far the dark pixels of the boxed label lie from each
edge (5.0, 5.0, 6.0 and 4.25 pt: left, top, right, bottom), found all four inside the allowed 6 pt,
saw no other label in the crop, and kept the estimate unchanged. So the record's region is an
estimate that passed a measured test; no script, rule or formula produced it.

measurement: the same 4 times render and the same margins. The control in this task therefore has
two parts: the crop of the recorded region must be byte-identical to the K4c crop, and the label box

control.unit: PDF points, frame pdf_display_page_top_left_points, [x0, y0, x1, y1]
rule: Render a window of 96 x 48 pt around a point inside the label at 4 times. A pixel is ink when its
grey level is below 128. The label box is the one group of touching ink pixels whose box holds the
point and holds another group (the frame around the characters). The region is that box widened by
the four K4c margins. Outside the label box and a soft edge of 0.5 pt the region must hold nothing
darker than grey 224. The crop of the recorded region must have the K4c crop's SHA-256.
whatItProves: The 4 times render, the meaning of "ink" and the four margins are K4c's: the label box is found from
the sheet without using the recorded numbers, and adding the margins K4c reported gives the recorded
numbers with no difference. It does not prove that a rule produced the recorded region; step0 says
inkLevel: K4c did not record the grey level it called ink. Levels 108, 128 and 144 all reproduce the recorded
region (exit 0 with --ink-below); 160 gives [595.75, 390, 644.25, 409] (exit 1). A scratch loop over
the committed functions in steps of 4 found 108 to 144 reproduce and nothing outside does. UNIT-3B
alone cannot say which level in that range is the right one.
